A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material reorganized between sections.

before.justification: V2 reports original training and robustness experiments on MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR10, including accuracy tables, training times, and illustrative experiments.

after.justification: V3 reports original convolutional-network experiments on four datasets, training times, and ablations of loss weighting, input sets, and set propagation.

M1.justification: V3 Appendix A(d) introduces substantial scalability adaptations: propagating approximation errors as intervals and constructing zonotopic training inputs from multiple adversarial attacks. V2 instead specifies full infinity-norm input balls and additional error generators at nonlinear layers. The core loss and gradient formulas remain. Separately, v3 Algorithm 1 adds the error midpoint before adding the uncentered error interval, introducing an inconsistency with the retained enclosure derivation.

E1.justification: V3 retains MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR10 and adds TinyImageNet. Its 100,000 images, 64-by-64 resolution, and 200 object classes materially extend the represented data and classification coverage beyond v2.

E2.justification: V2's main accuracy comparisons include Point, PGD, TRADES, IBP, SABR, and literature results from Mirman et al. V3 Table I retains only TRADES, IBP, and SABR as comparators to Set. Point remains in the toy and timing comparisons. V3 also introduces training comparisons against Set(Singh) and Set(IBP) propagation variants in Table IV.

E3.justification: V3 replaces the fully connected network-size grid with CNN6 for main experiments and CNN3 for ablations, including batch normalization. Training schedules, learning rates, batch sizes, and loss weights change substantially; CIFAR10 gains crop/flip augmentation. Verification of IBP and SABR changes from interval propagation to zonotopes. These are revised experimental conditions, not directly comparable reruns of v2.

E4.justification: V3 adds three design ablations: robustness-loss weighting, infinity-norm versus FGSM-derived input sets, and alternative set-propagation methods (Tables II–IV). The earlier decision-boundary and enclosure examples are retained, while v2's perturbation-radius curves disappear. The new ablations substantially expand evidence about design choices.

E5.justification: V2 averages accuracies over ten runs and displays plus/minus values. V3 reports explicitly labeled means and standard deviations for the best three of five seeds, without specifying the selection criterion, and adds maximum fast-verified accuracies. Timing summaries also change from ten-run averages to five-run minima. This substantially changes statistical reporting and aggregation.

E6.justification: The main accuracy and timing results are largely replaced. For example, v2 Table II reports 85.36% verified MNIST accuracy for Set with nn-large; v3 Table I reports 95.86% for CNN6 under different settings, so this is not a same-setting gain. V3 adds TinyImageNet results, including 0.02% fast-verified accuracy for Set, and new ablation results; the old architecture grid and CIFAR10 timing results are removed.

T1.justification: V3 adds an explicit operation-counting convention and changes Proposition 3's Minkowski-sum complexity from O(n(n+q)) to O(n), updating the corresponding complexity proof. The main enclosure theorem and gradient derivations are retained, largely condensed or relocated. The new outer-product notation restates the existing parameter-update mathematics.

C1.justification: V2's abstract and conclusion claim that set-based training consistently matches or outperforms state-of-the-art approaches; v3 narrows this to competitive performance. Novelty is framed more specifically around the first use of gradient sets and direct control of enclosure size. The central contribution of robust training supporting fast verification remains.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations linking smaller attack-derived input sets and poor interval-propagation performance to approximation-induced over-regularization. It replaces v2's interpretation of improving verification with network size with discussion of accuracy–verification tradeoffs. The fully connected-only limitation disappears following CNN evaluation, while the fundamental output-shrinkage explanation is retained.

D1.justification: V3 supplies CNN layer configurations, batch-normalization placement, revised hyperparameter tables, gradient clipping, augmentation, and scalability procedures. However, it removes v2's exact normalization constants and the reproduction instructions for the retained decision-boundary and enclosure figures, including the toy dataset and specific MNIST example. Reproducibility documentation changes substantially in both directions.

R1.justification: V3 adds related work on combining certified and adversarial training and on latent-space training, contrasting these approaches with gradient sets. References and discussion of input-gradient regularization and distillation are removed, while TinyImageNet and augmentation-related references are added. The broader positioning within robust training and verification remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, contributions, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around gradient sets. Training and loss now precede the detailed propagation machinery; related-work subsections are reorganized, and proofs are consolidated into Appendix B. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: V3 adds the introductory gradient-comparison diagram, removes v2's forward/backpropagation diagram and accuracy curves, and relocates retained illustrations. Separate dataset accuracy tables are replaced by a combined table with maximum-score reporting. New ablation and hyperparameter tables, revised architecture/timing tables, and reformatted algorithms substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: CNN evaluation addresses v2's fully connected-only limitation, while TinyImageNet and design ablations strengthen empirical coverage. However, v3 replaces ten-run averages with selectively reported best-three-of-five summaries and removes reproduction details for retained figures. Algorithm 1 also introduces a duplicated error-midpoint shift absent from v2, conflicting with the retained enclosure formula. The PDFs do not establish whether this inconsistency affects implementation. These material benefits and unresolved harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
